In support of this hypothesis, transgenic mice displaying suppressed levels of selenoproteins (a class of proteins that act as powerful antioxidants) had 50% more muscle mass following synergist ablation compared to wild-type controls (1 12). Moreover, supplementation with antioxidants that inhibit ROS production impairs both intracellular anabolic signaling and muscle hypertrophy following muscular overload (181). Collectively, these findings suggest that redox-sensitive signaling pathways may enhance exercise-induced muscular adaptations.
